approved: Introduced a bill abolishing the Clean Energy Finance Corporation with a transitional period of up to six months, longer than the previous bill's 28 days, transferring its assets and liabilities to the Commonwealth and returning future funding due until 2017 to consolidated revenue.

Opposed the carbon tax repeal, citing that renewable energy produced over 14 per cent of Australia's power in 2013 and more than two million households had installed clean energy systems, and cited modelling finding the renewable energy target would save households more than $500 million on power bills by 2020.
Moved to vary the House's 24 June resolution on the carbon tax repeal package so that the Clean Energy Finance Corporation Abolition Bill would be excluded and considered instead at the next sitting.
